extracted.intended_audience: mathematics teacher educators, in-service secondary mathematics teachers, college-level mathematics instructors, and mathematics education researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating case-based professional development and measurement (IDI) to build intercultural competence for mathematics instruction in secondary and tertiary settings, including stage descriptions and case-prompt guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional characteristic 1: obligation of service ('calling')
rubrics_metrics.description: the obligations of service to others, as in a 'calling'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed by Shulman as a defining characteristic of a profession; frames teacher work as service-oriented and has cultural implications for professional education and expectation-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional characteristic 2: theoretical understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: understanding of a scholarly or theoretical kind [e.g., mathematics, pedagogy]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses the need for content and pedagogical knowledge in pre-service and in-service teacher education; ties to degree expectations and ongoing PD focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional characteristic 3: domain of skilled performance
rubrics_metrics.description: a domain of skilled performance or practice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports the development of competent instructional practice and is a target for observation protocols and professional learning communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional characteristic 4: exercise of judgment under unavoidable uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: the exercise of judgment under conditions of unavoidable uncertainty [e.g., instructional decision-making in classroom contexts]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights that teachers must make context-dependent technical and moral judgments; suggests teacher education should prepare teachers for real-world uncertain decision-making rather than only idealized situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional characteristic 5: need for learning from experience
rubrics_metrics.description: the need for learning from experience as theory and practice interact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates reflective practice and case-based learning are important; suggests the design of PD should include mechanisms for learning from classroom experience (cases, reflection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional characteristic 6: professional community for quality monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: a professional community to monitor quality and aggregate knowledge
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports use of professional learning communities and communal storage/exchange of cases and experiences as a quality-control and knowledge-aggregation mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short definition of culture
rubrics_metrics.description: A dynamic social system of values, beliefs, behaviors, and norms for a specific group, organization, or other collectivity; the shared values, beliefs, behaviors, and norms are learned, internalized, and changeable by members of the society (Hammer, 2009).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this operational definition when constructing case materials or prompts; frames culture broadly to include professional/classroom environments and personal/home experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural alignment approach
rubrics_metrics.description: An approach where a teacher is supported to offer instruction in ways aligned with the homogeneous, 'local' culture of students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach can under-attend to the uncertainty inherent in heterogeneity; useful when classrooms are culturally homogeneous but may fail in diverse settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom participation approach
rubrics_metrics.description: An approach where curricula derived from majority-group normative policies drive learning activity and the teacher is expected to provide acculturative support that 'might enable particular groups of students to participate substantially in these activities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While enabling participation in mainstream activities, this approach can under-attend the uncertainty inherent in heterogeneity and may ignore negotiation among multiple cultural perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developmental Model orientation — Denial (innocent/bemused)
rubrics_metrics.description: Left endpoint orientation: lens based in the assumption 'Everybody is like me.' May notice observable differences but not deeper values/beliefs; often avoids or expresses disinterest in cultural difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Called 'denial' in some literature; in classroom examples this is shown by an instructor focusing on a preferred representation without noticing deeper cultural/communicative differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developmental Model orientation — Polarization
rubrics_metrics.description: Driven by the assimilative assumption 'Everybody should be like me/my group'; views cultural differences as 'us' vs 'them.' Polarization can take the form of 'defense' (uncritical view of one's group, overly critical of others) or 'reversal' (uncritical view of others, negative view of own group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In examples, polarization shows up as constant comparison and focus on differences; can lead to preference for one's own representation and resistance to others' approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developmental Model orientation — Minimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Lens based on 'Despite some differences, we really are all the same, deep down.' Attends to similarity and universals but is blind to deeper differences; may confuse empathy with sympathy and assume commonality without relational validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimization can foster shared feeling of understanding but risks missing nuanced cultural differences that affect communication and problem solving in mathematics contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developmental Model orientation — Acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Socio-cultural 'acceptance' as consenting to receive: mindfulness of self as having a culture and awareness of moving among multiple cultures; supports empathy and contextual awareness, though in-the-moment responses may still be elusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance enables recognition of difference and context but may need further development (adaptation) to shift behavior responsively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developmental Model orientation — Adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: An orientation where one develops culture-general frameworks for perception and behavior shifts responsive to full-spectrum detail in intercultural interaction; one may shift cultural perspective without losing authenticity and adjust communication appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adaptation represents advanced intercultural competence where communicative behavior is adaptively tuned to context and others' perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuum transitions and dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitions: noticing difference → seeking commonality → attending to nuance → context-based shifting. Movement along the continuum is not direct or linear; folding back to previous orientations (particularly under stress) is common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case materials and PD should attend to transition activities and accept non-linear development; emphasize the value of learning during transitions and occasional folding back.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intercultural Development Inventory (IDI) instrument and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: IDI: 50 Likert-like items and 4 open response items; elicits developmental orientation (most likely orientation in day-to-day interactions), perceived orientation, trailing orientations (fallbacks under stress), and leading orientation (edge for development). Open items ask for stories about intercultural exchanges that went well or poorly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IDI to get quantitative overview of orientations and qualitative material for case stories; IDI profiles can guide selection or design of case prompts targeted to participants' developmental needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case as pedagogical device (features of an effective case)
rubrics_metrics.description: A case is a context-rich description in words, images, or both, of a dilemma, challenge, or epitome. An effective case generates dissonance between what users thought they knew and what they witness, creating a basis for new understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases should be situated, draw together theory and practice, present morally/technically ambiguous situations, and serve as material for both individual reflection and community discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case prompts — four key areas to draw attention to
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompts are especially effective if they draw attention to: (1) Framing — analyze different interpretations; (2) Strategizing — evaluate actions of participants and oneself and how intentions become actions; (3) Connecting — identify and relate personal experiences to the case; (4) Forecasting — predict consequences of actions/inactions for participants and self in immediate and longer term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design prompts to target framing, strategizing, connecting, and forecasting; use them to surface developmental, perceived, and leading orientations and to facilitate discussion of transitions among orientations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt complexity and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompts may call upon complex synthesis, evaluation, and analysis of multiple sources, but can also be simple (e.g., 'Describe the problem... What might you do...? Illustrate your strategy... What are the risks and consequences?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match prompt complexity to the vignette's intricacy and intended method of response (writing, discussion); include explicit requests for examples and risk assessment to spur deeper reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three common debriefing goals for participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Common goals that emerged: (1) build awareness of self as having a cultural lens for viewing the world; (2) find guidance in transitions through minimization into acceptance, especially being mindful of one's cultural filter(s); (3) build a knowledge base about equity, including culturally normative values and distinguishing these from essentializing/stereotyping approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these goals to shape case selection, prompts, and debrief activities; explicitly target awareness, transition strategies, and critical knowledge about equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of narrative matrices to unpack interactions (Figure 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unpacking scenarios into columns showing actions, perspectives, utterances, and thoughts for each participant (and alternate endings) helps organize perceptions and supports reflection on multiple orientations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide matrix/unpacking to participants to reveal relational comparisons and different interpretive frames; use bold/italic conventions to distinguish utterances vs thoughts if helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anchoring case activities in intercultural competence development
rubrics_metrics.description: Case activities (e.g., points for discussion) should be anchored in intercultural competence concepts such as the developmental continuum and transition activities (noticing difference, seeking commonality, attending to nuance, context-based shifting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing cases, design prompts and debriefs that explicitly reference stages and transitions so participants can map their experiences onto the developmental model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: modify IDI for mathematics contexts ('math hat')
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask teachers/professors to take the IDI with a focus on mathematics as the culture being assumed in answering each item, and include an explicit question connecting culture and mathematics (e.g., comment on a provided story and offer your own).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This modified use of the IDI can produce richer material for math-specific case stories and professional development scenarios by eliciting responses framed by mathematical culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designing case characters and endings to target orientations
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct case characters (e.g., teacher in denial, student in polarization/minimization) and alternate endings that reveal leading orientations to provoke recognition and discussion among participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use characters positioned at different points on the continuum to create cognitive dissonance and to prompt participants to see themselves and colleagues in the descriptions; alternate endings can illustrate how leading orientations change outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of reflecting on transition activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Paying attention to transition activities—noting difference, seeing commonality, seeking nuance, and attending to multiple orientations—helps participants be reflective about themselves and their interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage participants to explicitly practice and reflect on these micro-activities during case discussions to support movement along the intercultural development continuum.
